{{Recipe}}

'''Firire''' is a dish loved by most Senegalese people. It is usually eaten as dinner and can be served with bread or fresh green salad.

== Ingredients ==

* Whole [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]], cleaned 
* 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]]
* 1 tablespoon [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]]
* [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|Chile powder]]
* Ground red pepper to taste
* 1 medium-sized (250 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
* [[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste 
* [[Cookbook:Oil and Fat|Oil]] for frying 
* ½ green pepper, [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]] along its length 
* [[Cookbook:Lettuce|Lettuce]]
* 1 medium-sized [[Cookbook:Cucumber|cucumber]], peeled and sliced 
* [[Cookbook:Plantain|Plantain]], peeled and sliced 
* 2 medium-sized cherry [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]

== Procedure ==

# Wash the fish very well and make slashes along the body.
# Combine the garlic, mustard, vinegar, chile powder, red pepper, onions, and a pinch of salt. Rub on the fish, and leave to [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinate]] for 15 minutes.
# Scrape the onions off the fish, and reserve them.
# Heat the oil in a pan over moderate heat. Add the fish, and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] on both sides until browned. Remove and set aside.
# Add the marinated onions to the pan. Fry until browned, stirring every 2–3 minutes. 
# Stir in the green pepper. Reduce the heat to medium, and cook for about 7 minutes. Set aside this sauce.
# Combine a dash of vinegar, oil, and mustard to make a dressing. [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|Toss]] the dressing with the lettuce and cucumber. Set aside
# Fry the plantain, and season with salt to taste.
# Arrange the salad in a dish, and place the fish in the center. [[Cookbook:Garnish|Garnish]] with tomatoes and plantains. Serve with the reserved sauce.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You can enjoy the firire with [[Cookbook:Bread|bread]] instead of plantains. It is also excellent with mayonnaise.
